summary: Source Workbench GUI and PWDT Library writes share canonical source/membership and selection admission for project update/deletion, model save/save-as/deletion and version rename/deletion. Fresh project creation is authority-fenced without requiring an existing catalog. Late old-source confirmations cannot reconcile same-ID new-source records, refresh the new backend or continue dependent PWDT writes; confirmed original outcomes remain contextChanged and same-source deletion cleanup stays independent of newer workspace ownership. Version history is passed canonically through composition and the typed invoker. GUI serialization follows admission, old-source errors suppress publication, verified history can recover independently of a blocked project catalog, and read recovery does not replay writes. Pure frontend and mocked Chromium evidence qualifies source-client contract/recovery/UX, not authenticated identity, continuous authority/membership or payload provenance, write exclusion, audit-routing ownership, installed WebView, remote execution, numerical accuracy or exactly-once. No operational-grade promotion, backup, snapshot or production Node dependency.
